caption: If you want to read more, there’s a brilliant piece on Substack titled “You F*ck the Way You Spend Money” I didn’t write it but I HIGHLY recommend it. #wealthbuilding #richwomen #wealthishealth #moneymagic #forthegirls
author: Sky Fisher
transcript: A very wealthy woman taught me this. Women's relationship with wealth is governed by three key things. Pleasure, power, and death. You're a portal for life. Your relationship with death is exemplified through your relationship to endings. It can be as simple as the death of an old version of yourself that you allow to end gracefully, that you bury and move forward, versus making that corpse something that you drag everywhere with you, the rancid smell of the version of yourself that you cannot let go of, filling up every single room, no matter how you wish to present yourself defiling the place, because you cannot just let it go. Your relationship with death must be one that is sacred and regularly honored, one that does not insist upon dragging the dead things around with you like a hunter who keeps every single trophy kill he's ever made on his back because he's afraid that more will never come. Your relationship with power is incredibly important because everyone understands intrinsically that money is power, but women have been taught to run from power. We have been punished every time we attain power. It's very likely that you and every single woman in your bloodline has been punished for trying to get power. Women have been taught to self-sabotage as an act of self-preservation, and it shows up. It shows up in your inability to provide for yourself, in your inability to accept power and responsibility, in your aversion to taking accountability in all of these ways, but most especially in your bank account. Finally, pleasure. This shows up really well in your sex life. Are you capable of asking for what you want and enjoying it without keeping tally of what you owe? Do you allow yourself to sit in that intense experience of desire between wanting and having, or do you rush from one to the other too quickly to exist and meditate on that feeling of want? There is a discomfort in abundance for people who have always lived in scarcity. It's like sitting at a table full of food that you know you will not be able to eat, and sitting with that feeling. Does shame come up? Does guilt? Does grief? The understanding that waste will occur and accepting that that happens and that it does not demarcate you as a bad person. Accepting, in fact, that abundance will replace abundance and you will not lose anything for having eaten as much as you wanted and stopped instead of gorging yourself on what presents itself in the moment because you anticipate that scarcity will follow abundance every time. I have a lot more I could say about this, but I'll quit while I'm ahead. Bye.
title: Women's Wealth Blocks: Pleasure, Power, Death
one_liner: Women's relationship with wealth is rooted in unresolved patterns around death, power, and pleasure.
key_points: Clinging to old versions of yourself (not honoring endings) blocks financial growth
Women are conditioned to self-sabotage as self-preservation after being punished for attaining power
Inability to sit with desire or abundance — rushing from want to having — reflects a scarcity mindset
Shame and guilt around waste signal a deep belief that abundance will always be followed by scarcity
